newsitem.title: SWEDEN: New S-E-Banken board member quiet on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: New S-E-Banken board member quiet on merger talk.

text.p: Swedish business leader Claes Dahlback, soon to join the board of S-E-Banken, on Tuesday would not comment on the possibility of new merger discussions between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken.
"I have no comment on any eventual cooperation between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken," Dahlback told reporters at a seminar on EMU and Swedish business.
Merger talks between S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken collapsed earlier this year.
But since then there has been a change of guard at S-E-Banken, which is seen as a Wallenberg family bank.
Jacob Wallenberg has been appointed to replace Bjorn Svedberg as chief executive and Dahlback, managing director of the Wallenberg's investment vehicle Investor, appointed to the board.
Nordbanken has said it would be willing to restart merger talks.
Dahlback confirmed that Investor had bought a batch of shares in S-E-Banken.
"We see possibilities in the restructuring changes in the bank and financial sector in the near future," he said.
But he would not be drawn on newspaper reports that he was to be made the new chairman of S-E-Banken. The bank has already announced that he is to join the board.
Dagens Nyheter said he would be appointed vice chairman this year then replace Karl-Erik Sahlberg when he retires next year aged 70.
"I have not been consulted about the chairmanship at S-E-Banken," Dahlback said.
